answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded answer): In the requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems survey (276 respondents; 194 valid Q8 respondents after excluding 82 suspended block non-respondents coded -77), the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are **Project Lead/Project Manager** (99/194 = 51.031% of respondents reported this role as "quoted"/addressing ML aspects; bootstrap mean 50.985%, 95% CI [43.814%, 58.247%]) and **Data Scientist** (95/194 = 48.969%; bootstrap mean 48.989%, 95% CI [41.753%, 56.186%]). All 8 Q8_ML_Addressing_* role items were computed with denominator = item respondents (194); "Others" (free-text catch-all) was reported but excluded from the two-role answer: Business Analyst 25.773% [19.588, 31.959], Developer 19.072% [13.918, 24.742], Solution Architect 12.371% [7.732, 17.010], Requirements Engineer 10.309% [6.186, 14.433], Others 9.794% [5.670, 13.918], Test Manager/Tester 1.031% [0.000, 2.577]. Bootstrap: respondent-level resampling with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42, percentile 95% CI. The top-2 identity is robust to subsetting: excluding suspended respondents and requiring ≥1 completed ML project (D7_Total_ML_Projects > 0, n=171) still ranks Project Lead/Project Manager first (93/171 = 54.386%, CI [46.784, 61.404]) and Data Scientist second (89/171 = 52.047%, CI [44.444, 59.649]); the same top-2 held under all denominators tested (276, 194, 188, 164). Note: the question's cited figures of 49.6% (95% CI [49.219, 49.981]) and 61.389% (95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) do not reproduce from this raw file under any tested denominator or subsetting — the data show 51.031% and 48.969% with CIs of ~±7 points (expected for n=194), whereas the cited CIs are ~±0.4 points, suggesting the source analysis used a different subset, coding, or resampling scheme; however, the identity of the two most-associated roles (Project Lead/Project Manager and Data Scientist) is consistent with the question and is not sensitive to the subsetting choices tested.

payload.hypothesis: In the requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems survey, the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are Project Lead/Project Manager (51.031%; 99/194 valid respondents; bootstrap 95% CI [43.814, 58.247]) and Data Scientist (48.969%; 95/194; bootstrap 95% CI [41.753, 56.186]). The Q8 role items are binary ('quoted'/'not quoted'); '-77' (82 suspended respondents) was treated as no response and excluded, giving denominator 194. Bootstrap: respondent-level resampling with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42, percentile 95% CI. The top-2 identity is robust to subsetting (still Project Lead then Data Scientist when excluding suspended respondents and requiring >=1 completed ML project, n=171: 54.386% CI [46.784, 61.404] and 52.047% CI [44.444, 59.649]). The question's cited 49.6% (CI [49.219, 49.981]) and 61.389% (CI [60.955, 61.822]) do not reproduce from this raw file under tested denominators; the data-grounded figures above are reported instead, while the two-role identity matches.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 rows x 202 cols). 2) Identified Q8_ML_Addressing_* role items as tri-state ('quoted'/'not quoted'/'-77'); -77 = 82 suspended block non-respondents, excluded (valid n=194). 3) Computed per-role 'quoted' proportions over item respondents (194) for all 8 roles incl. Others. 4) Respondent-level nonparametric bootstrap, B=10000, seed=42, percentile 95% CI. 5) Sensitivity subset: excluded suspended status and required D7_Total_ML_Projects>0 (n=171); ranking unchanged. 6) Ranked roles; top-2 = Project Lead/Project Manager and Data Scientist; noted non-reproducibility of the question's embedded percentages.
